environment.deployment: Isolated local Docker Compose stack in DifyBench-Isolated-20260828

cases.name: late_ack_streaming_success_control
cases.observation: The measured task remained unacknowledged while its HTTP effect was blocked, then completed once and acknowledged normally after release.

cases.name: late_ack_whole_worker_container_kill_after_effect

fault.target: The whole worker container whose active unacknowledged task contained the exact workflow run id

cases.observation_discontinuity: The isolated WSL runtime was externally stopped and later resumed, so no exact 120-second redelivery-latency claim is made.
cases.observation: The expired Redis unacked delivery survived whole-container loss. On a later cold worker start, the same Celery task id was received with redelivered=true and applied the external effect a second time before the run eventually succeeded.
does_not_prove: Redelivery exactly at the configured 120-second timeout

invalidated_attempts.reason: Incorrect client-container entrypoint; no workflow run, task, broker delivery, or effect was created.

key_finding: In this local Dify 1.16.1 Published streaming case, late ACK preserved a broker recovery path that the separately measured early-ACK default did not have. That recovery replayed the whole workflow task and duplicated a non-idempotent external side effect. Broker recoverability therefore did not provide exactly-once execution.
runtime_notes: A read-only experiment overlay changed only the target task annotation and the three Celery Redis visibility-timeout settings; effective API, worker, remote-worker, and live-channel values were captured before the run.

The overlay was removed and related services were recreated after evidence capture. The retained post-rollback runtime snapshot independently reverifies the worker's default early-ACK and transport settings; equivalent post-rollback runtime snapshots for API, websocket, and beat were not archived. Restoration of the original ext_celery.py hash was an operator terminal observation that was not independently archived. Both WSL distributions were left stopped without deleting retained data.
Whole-container loss removed the Celery parent process, so this run is attributed to Redis broker restoration on cold worker start and does not isolate task_reject_on_worker_lost.

The fixed Dify worker entrypoint defaults to gevent, and the measured Dummy-* execution context did not establish a separately killable OS pool child. A prefork variant would be a new experiment variable.
This is a local framework benchmark, not production experience or a production reliability guarantee.
single_next_experiment: In the isolated stack only, run a no-fault prefork feasibility and normal-control slice first. Explicitly set prefork with concurrency 1, retain the exact-task late-ACK annotation, use a visibility timeout longer than the control window, archive final worker argv, pool stats, the OS parent/child tree, and the exact task child PID, then prove a new blocking/release streaming control succeeds once and clears unacked state. Treat the pool change and Dify's gevent-patched celery_entrypoint as new variables. Stop without fault injection if a real child is absent or the control is unstable; only a later slice may kill the exact child to isolate reject-on-worker-lost.
